note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a SA 5(1)-(3); A06b SA 5(1)-(3); L05 SA 6(1), 6(2)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. On 6 May 2025 the Constitutional Court confirmed the declaration that section 6(1)(a) of the Citizenship Act, under which a citizen lost South African citizenship on voluntarily acquiring another, is invalid (Democratic Alliance v Minister of Home Affairs, as EWN reported it the same day), so a South African now keeps it on taking another.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, South Africa, 2024
sources.said: Person is a permanent resident and has been ordinarily and legally resident for at least 5 years. ... n.a. ... Person voluntarily acquires another citizenship and does not apply in advance to retain South African citizenship.

sources.title: EWN, ConCourt confirms declaration of constitutional invalidity for parts of Citizenship Act (6 May 2025)
sources.said: The Constitutional Court has confirmed the declaration of constitutional invalidity of s 6(1)(a) of the Citizenship Act. The section stipulates that South African citizens lose their citizenship after voluntarily acquiring the citizenship of another country.
